# Taxonomy of Grid-Based Logic Games

## Primary Categories

---

## 1. LOOP/PATH DRAWING GAMES
*Games where the primary action is drawing a continuous line or loop*

### 1.1 Pure Loop Games
*Single loop with geometric/structural constraints*
- **Slitherlink** — Loop drawn between dots; numbers count surrounding edges
- **Masyu** — Loop through all circles; black/white circles impose turn/straight rules
- **Mid-loop** — Loop passes through black circles, which must be midpoints of straight segments
- **Nagareru** — Directional loop; wind constraints force or forbid movement directions

### 1.2 Loop Games with Room/Area Constraints
*Loop must respect bounded regions*
- **Moon-or-Sun** — Loop passes through rooms once; alternates between moon and sun cells
- **Suraromu** — Loop passes through all "Gates" exactly once; numbered gates constrain crossing order
- **Dotchi-Loop** — Loop through white circles; all circles in a bold-line area must be either all straight or all turns

### 1.3 Loop Games with Cell Marking Constraints
*Loop interacts with black cells or directional clues*
- **Yajilin** — Loop avoids black cells and numbered arrow cells; arrows count black cells in their direction
- **Numberlink** — Connect matching number pairs with non-crossing, non-overlapping paths

---

## 2. REGION/AREA DIVISION GAMES
*Games where the primary action is dividing the grid into regions or blocks*

### 2.1 Division by Shape Rules
*Regions must conform to specific shapes*
- **Shikaku** — Divide into rectangles; each contains exactly one number indicating its cell count
- **Sashigane** — Divide into L-shaped blocks; circles mark bends, arrows point toward bends
- **LITS** — Color one tetromino per region; same-shaped tetrominoes cannot touch; colored cells connect
- **Fillomino** — Fill grid with numbered blocks; block size equals its number; same-size blocks cannot touch

### 2.2 Division with Paired/Symmetric Regions
*Regions must contain matching sub-areas*
- **Double Choco** — Divide into blocks each containing equal white and gray areas of identical shape
- **Nuritwin** — Each outlined region contains exactly two same-sized shaded blocks; blocks connect across regions

### 2.3 Division into Fixed-Size Blocks
- **Five Cells** — Divide grid into blocks of exactly five cells; numbers count surrounding block-boundary lines
- **Norinori** — Each bold-line area contains exactly two consecutive black squares (dominoes)

---

## 3. CELL COLORING/SHADING GAMES
*Games where the primary action is painting or coloring individual cells black*

### 3.1 Coloring with Connectivity Rules
*Black and/or white cells must form connected or disconnected patterns*
- **Nurikabe** — Black cells form a connected wall; white cell islands contain exactly one number matching island size
- **Heyawake** — Paint cells in rooms per number; no two painted cells touch; white cells cannot span more than two rooms
- **Hitori** — Paint cells so no number repeats in any row/column; black cells don't touch; white cells stay connected
- **Kurodoko** — Paint cells black; numbered white cells count visible white cells in four directions; black cells don't touch

### 3.2 Coloring with Shape Constraints
*Black/white regions must form or avoid specific shapes*
- **Choco Banana** — Black cells form rectangles/squares; white cells must NOT form rectangles/squares; numbers count area size
- **Shakashaka** — Place triangles in cells so remaining white areas always form rectangles/squares; numbers count adjacent triangles
- **Usowan** — Paint cells; numbers count adjacent painted cells but exactly one number per bold-line rectangle is wrong

### 3.3 Coloring with Sum/Count Rules
- **Kurotto** — Numbers in circles indicate sum of continuous black cells extending from circle in four directions
- **Sto-stone** — Paint cells in rooms per count; when "dropped" downward, painted cells fill exactly the bottom half
- **Tilepaint** — Color entire tiles; diagonal-number cells count black cells rightward or downward to grid edge or next diagonal

### 3.4 Coloring as Maze Construction
- **Nurimeizu** — Paint whole rooms to create walls; white cells form a maze from S to G; circles on shortest path, triangles off it

---

## 4. NUMBER/SYMBOL PLACEMENT GAMES
*Games where the primary action is filling cells with numbers or symbols*

### 4.1 Latin Square / Uniqueness Constraints
*Numbers must be unique within rows, columns, or regions*
- **Sudoku** — Place 1–9 in each row, column, and 3×3 box
- **Makaro** — Each room contains 1 through N (room size); arrow cells point to their largest neighbor; no same number adjacent across rooms
- **Ripple Effect** — Each room contains 1 through N; duplicate numbers in a row/column must be separated by at least that number of cells

### 4.2 Consecutive/Sequential Placement
*Numbers must follow a sequence or path*
- **Hebi** — Place 1–5 sequentially to form snakes; snakes cannot touch each other; directional clues in black cells
- **Nansuke** — Fill blank cells with digits from a given number list; numbers read horizontally or vertically

### 4.3 Symbol/Mark Filling
- **Juosan** — Fill every cell with — or |; territory numbers show excess of one mark over the other; marks limited in perpendicular direction

---

## 5. CONNECTION/BRIDGE GAMES
*Games where the primary action is connecting nodes or islands*

- **Hashiwokakero** — Connect numbered islands with bridges matching each island's number; max two bridges between any pair; all islands connected
- **Yosenabe** — Move numbered circles into gray areas; arrow paths cannot cross; gray area numbers must match sum of entering circles

---

## 6. OBJECT PLACEMENT GAMES
*Games where the primary action is placing discrete objects into the grid*

### 6.1 Light/Visibility Placement
- **Akari** — Place light bulbs in white cells; numbered black cells count adjacent bulbs; every white cell must be illuminated; bulbs cannot see each other

### 6.2 Block/Shape Placement
- **Evolomino** — Place squares to form blocks on arrows; blocks grow by one square along arrow route without rotation/flipping
- **Pencils** — Identify pencil shapes and draw lines from tips; line length matches number in pencil

---

## 7. MOVEMENT/MIGRATION GAMES
*Games where existing objects are moved to satisfy constraints*

- **Satogaeri** — Move circles into their home "country" regions; numbered circles travel exact distances; paths cannot cross
- **Chained Block** — Fill cells to create numbered black-cell blocks; blocks touch at corners forming chains; no two same-shaped blocks in one chain

---

## 8. HYBRID / MULTI-MECHANIC GAMES
*Games combining two or more primary mechanics at equal weight*

### 8.1 Coloring + Loop
- **Nurimisaki** — Paint cells leaving "promontory" circles white with exactly one white neighbor; white cells connect; no 2×2 of either color

### 8.2 Division + Number Placement
- **Shikaku** *(see 2.1)* / **Fillomino** *(see 2.1)*

### 8.3 Loop + Coloring
- **Yajilin** *(see 1.3)* — Loop drawn while black cells are also placed

### 8.4 Path + Region
- **Dotchi-Loop** *(see 1.2)*
- **Moon-or-Sun** *(see 1.2)*

---

## Summary Table

| Category | Games |
|---|---|
| Loop/Path Drawing | Slitherlink, Masyu, Mid-loop, Nagareru, Moon-or-Sun, Suraromu, Dotchi-Loop, Yajilin, Numberlink |
| Region Division | Shikaku, Sashigane, LITS, Fillomino, Double Choco, Nuritwin, Five Cells, Norinori |
| Cell Coloring | Nurikabe, Heyawake, Hitori, Kurodoko, Choco Banana, Shakashaka, Usowan, Kurotto, Sto-stone, Tilepaint, Nurimeizu |
| Number/Symbol Placement | Sudoku, Makaro, Ripple Effect, Hebi, Nansuke, Juosan |
| Connection/Bridge | Hashiwokakero, Yosenabe |
| Object Placement | Akari, Evolomino, Pencils |
| Movement/Migration | Satogaeri, Chained Block |
| Hybrid | Nurimisaki |
